title: At a Cafe: Ordering Drinks and Paying
summary: You will learn how to order drinks and desserts at a cafe. You will also learn how to pay.

cover.alt: Cafe counter with hot and cold drinks, cake, cookie, cash, and a bank card under warm window light.

blocks.title: At the Cafe
paragraphs: You will learn how to order drinks and desserts at a cafe. You will also learn how to pay. A clear order helps the person serving you understand what you want.

items.prompt: What do you usually drink at a cafe?
Do you like cake or a cookie with your drink?
Do you usually pay by card or with cash?

blocks.title: Drinks and Something Sweet
paragraphs: A cafe order can start with a drink and something sweet. At the cafe, Maya serves hot coffee and cold tea. Coffee can come with milk, while the cold tea can come without sugar. These details matter because two people can order tea but want different drinks. A small cup holds less than a large cup. Maya also serves cake by the slice and cookies as separate pieces. A slice of cake and a cookie are two different dessert choices. One person might want only a drink, while another wants both. The drink, its size, and the dessert are separate parts of the order. Clear details help Maya prepare the right things.

items.prompt: A customer wants cold tea and something sweet. What details would help Maya prepare the order?
items.answer: Maya needs to know the size of the tea and whether the customer wants sugar. The customer also needs to choose a dessert, such as a slice of cake or a cookie.
items.explanation: The drink alone does not tell Maya its size, the sugar choice, or the dessert.

blocks.title: Choose Your Drink and Dessert
paragraphs: I'd like a small hot coffee, please.
A cold tea without sugar, please.
I'd like a slice of cake, too.
Just a cookie, please.

blocks.title: Build a Clear Order
paragraphs: An order is easier to follow when its details stay together. The drink name tells the cafe worker what to prepare. Words such as small, hot, and cold make that choice clearer. At the cafe, Leo takes an order for a small hot coffee with milk. He repeats the drink details before preparing it. The customer listens and confirms that the order is right. A dessert can follow as another part of the same order. Leo then adds a cookie for this customer. An order can also include whether the customer will stay or take it away. This customer will stay, so Leo now has the complete order.

items.prompt: Leo repeats “a large hot coffee with milk,” but the customer wants a small one. How can the customer correct the order?
items.answer: A small hot coffee with milk, please, not a large one.
items.explanation: The customer changes the size and keeps the other drink details clear.

blocks.title: Confirm or Change a Detail
paragraphs: A small one, please.
With milk, please.
Without sugar, please.
That's right, thank you.
To take away, please.
I'll stay here.

blocks.title: Pay for the Right Order
paragraphs: Payment comes after the order is clear. Here, Maya accepts both card and cash. A customer chooses how to pay before Maya finishes the sale. With cash, the customer gives money directly to Maya. With a card, the customer uses the card machine. The bill should match the food and drinks the customer ordered. In this example, Maya notices an extra cookie on the bill. She removes it before taking payment. The customer then pays by card and gets a receipt. Fixing the order first keeps the payment clear for both people.

items.prompt: Your bill includes a cookie you did not order. What should happen before you pay?
items.answer: I should explain that I did not order the cookie. Maya should remove it from the bill. Then I can pay for my correct order.
items.explanation: The bill needs to match the order before payment.

blocks.title: Pay and Fix a Small Mistake
paragraphs: Can I pay by card?
I'll pay with cash.
Sorry, I didn't order this cookie.
Just the coffee, please.
Could I have a receipt, please?

blocks.title: A Small Hot Drink
paragraphs: You are ordering a hot drink from Maya at the cafe counter, where coffee comes in small and large cups. You want a small hot coffee with milk to take away.
Your goal is to order the drink and confirm its size.

images.alt: Barista Maya and a customer at the counter with a small cup and a large cup for hot coffee size choices.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Hello! What would you like?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'd like a hot coffee with milk, please.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Small or large?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Small, please.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Will you stay here or take it away?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: To take away, please.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: That's a small hot coffee with milk to take away.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: That's right, thank you.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Here is your coffee.

blocks.title: Cold Tea and Cake
paragraphs: You are choosing a drink and dessert with Leo at the cafe, which serves cold tea and slices of cake. You want a small cold tea without sugar and a slice of cake to enjoy there.
Your goal is to order both items and make the sugar choice clear.

images.alt: Barista Leo serves cold tea and cake; sugar sits separate beside a small table.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Hello! What would you like?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: A small cold tea and a slice of cake, please.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Would you like sugar in your tea?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: No sugar, please.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Will you stay here?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, I'll stay here.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: So, a small cold tea without sugar and a slice of cake.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, that's right.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Here are your tea and cake. Enjoy!

blocks.title: A Small Mistake on the Bill
paragraphs: You are paying Maya at the cafe, where both card and cash are accepted. You ordered only a coffee, but the bill also includes a cookie.
Your goal is to remove the cookie from the bill, pay by card, and get a receipt.

images.alt: Maya and a customer fix a bill at the counter before paying by card.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Your bill is ready.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Sorry, I didn't order this cookie. Just the coffee, please.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: I'm sorry. I've removed the cookie. The bill now has only your coffee.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. Can I pay by card?

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Yes. We accept card and cash. Please use the card machine.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I've paid. Could I have a receipt, please?

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Your payment is complete. Here is your receipt.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. Goodbye!

items.prompt: You are placing an order at a cafe. Choose a coffee or tea and a cake slice or cookie. Say your complete order aloud, including size, hot or cold, and milk or sugar. Then say whether you will stay or take it away and how you want to pay.
items.explanation: The worker repeats the wrong size. Say a short correction aloud.

items.prompt: A clear cafe order includes the drink and the details you want. The bill should match your order before you pay. Which details matter most for your usual cafe order, and what would you say if the bill were wrong?

rows.meaning: Something you have from a cup or glass.

rows.example: I'd like a dessert with my tea.

rows.meaning: A flat piece cut from something larger.
A bank card used to pay for things.
A list showing what you need to pay for.
A record showing that you paid.
rows.example: Could I have a receipt, please?
